summary: Granite Co., MT site on Deerlodge NF: 1920s platform tower and cabin, 1932 L-4 tower, 1964 R-6 tower since removed; the log cabin remains.

facts.design: 20-foot treated timber R-6 flat tower (1964), since removed; earlier 20-foot pole L-4 tower (1932)
facts.status_note: The 1964 tower has been removed. Both sources say the 1920s log cabin remains, but neither dates that report, and a 1931 newspaper says lightning completely destroyed the lookout station that June.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Deerlodge National Forest

events.note: Pole platform tower with a log cabin; both sources date it to the 1920s without an exact year. A 1917 newspaper already describes a lookout station on the peak, so this tower was not the first.
A 20-foot pole L-4 tower replaced the 1920s platform tower and cabin
Jerry Churchwell served as a lookout in the summers of 1961-64
20-foot treated timber R-6 flat tower built by Driggs Construction of Anaconda, MT
Newspaper account: a woman took the post after a man quit, and watched through the summer
Lightning destroyed 1,500 feet of telephone line leading to the lookout station
June 1931: lightning struck a pack train on the slopes; the newspaper says the lookout station the men had just left was completely destroyed by the same bolt
Registered January 23, 2011 as US 827, MT 1; nominated by Luke Channer

corrections.why: The 1932 date is the L-4 tower that replaced the 1920s pole platform tower and log cabin, so the built date of that earlier structure is the 1920s. A 1917 newspaper already describes a lookout station on the peak, so the 1920s tower was not the first lookout there.

notes_for_editor: Coordinates: the record's 46.200267, -113.638933 match the FFLOS and firelookout.org points. The west_us_lookouts point (46.1877, -113.63369) is about 1.5 km to the south-southwest and was not used. WebSearch found nothing on Emerine. The cabin's present state rests on undated firelookout.com text and the FFLOS entry (registered 2011); no recent visit report or photo was found. No access or visit information in the sources. Newspaper quotes come from a secondary transcription on montanalookouts.weebly.com; the 1931 pack-train article carries an Independent (Helena) attribution in that transcription. Distances from Philipsburg differ across sources and are noted in the story.
